Hi Samira — thanks for the report and the clear asks. Looping Ben from pricing and Lauren from renewals to propose concrete options. High-level thoughts before we model numbers: 

Options we typically offer for a midterm surge:
1) Staged Top-up (preserve band): Buy a one-time top-up bucket at your current committed price; the top-up runs until your contract end date (co-term). This avoids blended rates but requires an upfront charge for the top-up capacity.
2) Blended Co-term Amend: Annualize the incremental usage into your base commit and compute a blended per-token rate for the remainder of the term; lower up-front but can nudge unit price depending on volume mix.
3) Voucher/Volume Credit: Issue a voucher equal to X% of the incremental spend to offset the higher blended price — useful when finance prefers amortized billing.

Can you confirm two pieces of data so we can run exact scenarios:
- Expected monthly token run-rate for Nov–Mar (rough monthly numbers or the delta on the attached report).
- Whether Arbor is willing/able to take an upfront invoice for a top-up vs. preferring amortization.

Ben, Lauren — I sketched the three levers above. Can you run 3 scenarios (top-up, blended annualize, and blended+voucher) and share worksheet (proposed_amend_v2.xlsx) with monthly cashflow and per-token "effective" price through 2027-03-31? Target to get that back to Arbor by 11/3 to meet their procurement window.

Samira — if it helps, we can schedule a 20-min call Thurs AM to walk the numbers live.

Best,

On Wed, Oct 28, 2026 at 10:01 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Ben, Lauren — I sketched the three levers above. Can you run 3 scenarios (top-up, blended annualize, and blended+voucher) and share worksheet...

Thanks Tessa — attaching an initial worksheet (proposed_amend_v2.xlsx) with scenario tabs. Quick summary of assumptions used for the model: 
- Baseline committed monthly tokens: 1.2B (per contract)
- Current overage rate band: $0.00090/token; committed rate: $0.00060/token
- Observed delta (Oct): +42% -> modeled incremental monthly delta: ~504M tokens (we used 500M for round numbers)

Summary outputs (high level):
- Top-up (one-time, preserve committed rate): Buy a 2.5B token top-up invoice now at $0.00060/token amortized to term end -> one-time invoice ~ $1.5M, spreads to effective uplift of +$0.00 (no unit premium) but cash impact up-front.
- Blended annualize: Incremental tokens folded into commit; blended rate for remainder of term rises to $0.000655/token (net effect: small increase vs committed but avoids large up-front).
- Blended + voucher: Provide a 12% voucher on incremental consumption (applied as credit over next 6 invoices) which moves blended effective price closer to committed (~$0.000615/token) and reduces immediate cash impact.

Notes/constraints:
- For co-terming, we can co-term with an amendment; legal lead time is typically 7–10 business days for a simple amendment (signatures + PO).
- Voucher approach needs AP alignment for crediting; finance prefers a clearly-delimited credit memo rather than open-ended discounts.

Tessa/Team — I flagged cells B24:B32 in the sheet where the customer-visible numbers live. Lauren, happy for you to own the amendment doc and timelines if we agree which scenario Arbor chooses.

Ben
Director, Commercial Pricing, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear scenarios. We reviewed the worksheet internally this morning with Finance + Legal. Arbor prefers option 3 (Blended + voucher) — the reduced up-front hit is important for our Q4 cash planning. A couple of follow-ups before we sign:

1) Can you confirm the voucher redemption schedule as a credit memo applied across 6 invoices starting after the amendment effective date?
2) We need the amendment to explicitly state: co-term to 2027-03-31; incremental tokens defined as "observed delta above baseline committed run-rate" (baseline = 1.2B); and a not-to-exceed cap on total voucher value (we propose $180k).
3) Timeline: if Redwood can provide the signed amendment PDF and a final invoice by 11/5 we can route the PO and sign on 11/8.

If you can confirm 1–3 and return the final amendment, we'll escalate to our procurement lead to get the PO out next week.

Appreciate the quick help.
Jordan Lee
